text:
The Indian market closed the week on a strong note, with the Nifty 50 up 2.61% to 25,800.6 and the Bank Nifty rallying 5.90% to 64,635.2, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 1.49% to 24,088.8. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers for the 17th straight session, adding INR 32,647 crore, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 12,698 crore for the third consecutive session. Breadth was “healthy” (score 69.9), 72% of stocks stayed above the 20‑day moving average and 86% were within 5% of their 52‑week highs, indicating wide‑scale participation.  

In IPO activity, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited opened its OFS on 19 Nov and will close on 23 Nov, with a price band of ₹129‑₹136; total subscription was 0.48 times, led by QIBs (1.37 ×). Recent listings showed mixed performance: BLS Polymers debuted at ₹150 and is now up 81% versus issue price, while SFC Environmental Technologies opened at ₹330 and is up 34% versus issue price. Other IPOs such as Bombay Coated & Special Steels and M.K. Sons Fine Jewels posted modest gains of 2.30% and 0.60% respectively.  

Looking ahead, the market may react to several catalysts. A weaker USD‑INR (down 1.46% to 92.66) and falling global commodity prices—Brent crude down 7.58% and gold down 8.05%—could support risk assets. However, higher volatility is signaled by the India VIX up 11.74% to 17.32, and overseas equity futures (S&P 500, Nasdaq 100) posted declines of over 5%, reflecting broader tech‑AI sell‑offs. Any shift in FII flows or domestic policy on foreign investment disclosures could also move the indices next week.
